sentence: This project builds a tool for use at home that measures the amount of tyrosine in the blood of people with inherited metabolic disorders.
This project studies how environmental exposures before birth, diet and cognitive stimulation affect how a child's brain develops.
This project studies how a recently found molecule controls the switch from fetal to adult hemoglobin in red blood cells.
This project provides brain imaging tools that help other research projects study how organophosphate intoxication harms the brain.
This project builds computer models that predict how T cell receptors recognize tumor antigens, using large sets of matched pairs.
This project tests whether infant thinking skills can be measured from home with remote testing methods.
This project studies how two lobes of the brain's cortex process information about faces, using electrophysiology and optical imaging.
This project studies how cells in articular cartilage control lipid metabolism and how this connects to a disease that degrades cartilage.
This project uses single-unit recordings during reversal learning to study how the external segment of the globus pallidus helps decision-making in obsessive-compulsive disorder.
This project studies how reduced motivation and pleasure in psychotic disorders relate to thinking and to connections between brain regions.
This project provides imaging and single-molecule methods to study how proteins interact with proteins, nucleic acids and membranes during the HIV life cycle.
This project compares immune genes in closely related primate species, rhesus and cynomolgus macaques, to find genes that affect susceptibility to tuberculosis.
This project uses deep learning on electronic health records to predict risk of rare disease in people who carry monogenic risk alleles.
This project studies how conflict between maternal and paternal genes on the X chromosome affects regulatory networks and gene transcription.
This project uses a mouse model of translocation renal cell carcinoma to find out how the cancer develops and to work toward treatments.
This project tests how well robotic-assisted bronchoscopy diagnoses lung ground glass nodules and builds models with spatial transcriptomics and radiomics.
This project studies how genes cause differences in the human immune response and in susceptibility to inhaled fungal infection.
This project builds a blood test that detects pancreatic cancer early in people at high risk and combines it with imaging and genetic data.
This project studies how a protein regulates the metabolism of T lymphocytes, which mediate immune responses against cancer.
This project studies how too much midasin helps estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer cells resist endocrine therapy.
